messages.text: I’m checking the lane brief, the replacement build and handback instructions, and the current `py08` worktree before changing anything. I’ll keep the implementation within the agreed two slices and report the evidence through the required handback.

The replacement procedure means I’ll build only through `cargo-slot`, keep all edits in `.worktrees/py08`, and avoid GitHub issue writes. The agreed design requires relational, SQL-readable format facts; I’m checking the architecture and existing structural/query persistence paths now to confirm what the two slices can add without duplicating the new binary or binding facts.

The existing format fixtures confirm the key false-positive case: `{0} {1}` with two arguments must stay clean while `{0}` with two arguments is surplus. Python’s normalizer already has `binary_expression` and call argument roles. The remaining integration question is where to combine a receiver’s literal initializer with py02’s lexical `BindingOf` result; I’m tracing that query boundary while setting down the required living plan.

I found a safe independent milestone: the decoded-value parsers can be built and tested without deciding how assignment origins join `BindingOf`. I’m implementing that parser layer first; the execution-plan record now captures the unresolved boundary so I can either integrate it through the existing binding facts or return a precise question if the query API cannot support it cleanly.

The parser milestone is in place with cases for escaped braces/percents, explicit and automatic fields, named fields, nested width fields, conversion slots, unsupported conversions, and malformed input. The focused Python-crate run is waiting for one of the three shared build slots; while it waits, I’m checking the smallest viable RQL integration points and whether they can invoke `BindingOf` without recursive structural fact loading.

The first parser run reached compilation but caught two test-only type mismatches in the unsupported-conversion expectations; I corrected those. The rerun is compiling through the shared slot now. The important design boundary remains: py02’s binding rows establish lexical identity, while the literal value requires a structured assignment join; I’m checking whether the existing structural query pipeline can supply that join without duplicating binding resolution.

The six focused parser tests now pass, and the repository-wide `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean. I’m keeping this checkpoint parser-only until the parent chooses the public operation/value-origin query boundary; that boundary determines how policy results and typed incompleteness are surfaced.

Checkpoint committed at `4482e2d223af28f37e652210451b9f235440281f`. Six parser tests and formatting checks pass. The eight rule integrations remain unfinished pending the parent’s choice of public query contract; the handback report includes the evidence and recommendation.

I’m resuming `py08` with the parent’s query-time design. I’ll inspect the current master-side `python_rule_fact` surface and py07’s concurrent exception-row edits first, then implement the format checks as grouped additions that reuse structural call/assignment facts and existing `BindingOf`.

I’m continuing from the parser checkpoint and integrating the findings into the existing typed Python rule-fact query path, following the parent’s query-time design. I’ll first refresh the relevant lane/worktree state, then implement the rows and policy fixtures before running the lane gate.

The current tree already has the PythonRuleFact terminal and both prerequisites. I’m adding one query step over selected structural calls and `%` binary nodes; each matching operation will emit a typed row per applicable rule, including explicit `no_issue` and `unknown` outcomes so unsupported shapes cannot look clean. The campaign’s not-mapping fixture uses a list RHS, so I’ve asked whether that shape should be classified as a known non-mapping while I proceed with the rest.

Thanks, that resolves the list case and tightens the mapping boundary. I’ll classify only the named built-in literal/container shapes as mapping or non-mapping, resolve `dict(...)` only when its builtin identity is structurally unshadowed, and leave every other dynamic RHS typed-incomplete.

The format parsers and row vocabulary are in place. I’m wiring the query step into the structural pipeline now, then I’ll add policy fixtures for the eight rules and the typed-incomplete cases before running the lane gate.

The query vocabulary is wired and both call and binary-expression inputs now reach the same query-local projection. The focused RQL test is waiting for the build slot; while it runs I’m keeping the lane changes isolated and will address any compile feedback before adding the policy cases.
